lit.'<p>Al descomponer la luz de una galaxia:
'

Splitting a galaxy’s light reveals spectral lines from elements such as hydrogen. In almost every galaxy those lines are shifted towards the red (longer wavelength): z = Δλ/λ. It is the sign that they are moving away from us. The most distant ones have the largest shift (graph «Spectrum»).

'
lit.'<p>El modelo del <b>Big Bang</b> descri:
'

The Big Bang model describes a universe that began very hot and dense and cooled as it expanded: light nuclei formed, then atoms (releasing the cosmic microwave background radiation), then the first stars, galaxies and, much later, the Solar System. Today the expansion is accelerating because of dark energy.

'
lit.'<p>En 1929 Edwin Hubble, con datos de V:
'

In 1929 Edwin Hubble, using data from Vesto Slipher and Henrietta Leavitt’s distance method, found that the recession velocity is proportional to distance: v = H₀·d. The Hubble constant is H₀ ≈ 70 km/s per megaparsec (1 Mpc ≈ 3.26 million light-years). Each point on the graph is a galaxy in the scene.

'
lit.'<p>La ley de Hubble no indica que estem:
'

Hubble’s law does not mean we are at the centre: it is space itself that expands, like raisin bread rising in the oven. From any galaxy (change the observer) the view is the same: all the others move away, the more distant ones faster. The universe has no centre.

'
lit.'<p>Mirar lejos es <b>mirar al pasado</b:
'

Looking far away is looking into the past: the light from a galaxy 1 billion light-years away left it 1 billion years ago. The Atacama Desert, with its dry air, high altitude and skies free of light pollution, hosts observatories such as ALMA, the VLT, the Vera C. Rubin and the future ELT, which study everything from star formation to the expansion of the universe.

'
lit.'<p>Si retrocedemos la película, las gal:
'

If we run the film backwards, the galaxies come together. A simple estimate of the age is the time each would take to reach its present distance: t ≈ d/v = 1/H₀. With H₀ = 70 km/s/Mpc it is ≈ 14 billion years; detailed calculations give 13.8 billion years.

'
